lua_optionsEmpty: Use an options object literal; timerClock accepts only 'level' or 'real'. You may also omit options and pass just the callback.
lua_invalidCallback: The script callback must return a lifecycle object directly. Write (lua) => { ...; return { ... } } or (lua) => ({ ... }).
lua_returnHooks: Return the lifecycle object directly at the end of the callback.
lua_publicMethodThis: Functions in methods are called by other scripts through Invoke as plain functions, so this is not bound to anything. Use the callback variables directly; methods inside a class can still use this.
lua_publicMethodName: methods may only contain functions written inline or declared in the callback, not class methods or other values. Method names also cannot clash with official lifecycle functions or global APIs.
lua_dynamicHooks: Declare lifecycle hooks such as onStart and onUpdate directly. Spreads and dynamically generated hooks are not supported.
lua_earlyReturn: The entry callback can only return its lifecycle object at the end.
lua_nestedEntry: A file may contain one top-level clientControlScript entry, with or without export default. Entries cannot be created inside functions.
lua_reservedEnv: _ENV is reserved for the Lua runtime environment. Choose another variable name.
lua_asyncFunction: Client Lua does not support async functions. Use ordinary callbacks, lifecycle hooks or timers.
lua_spreadEnvironment: You can pick out what you need by name, e.g. const { game, script } = lua, but you cannot spread the whole lua with ...lua.
lua_hostUnavailable: The engine's client Lua environment does not provide {{arg0}}. Use a supported native API or regular synchronous code.
lua_regexLiteral: Client Lua does not support JavaScript regular expression literals. Use lua.string.match or lua.string.gsub (Lua patterns), or ordinary string methods.
lua_generator: Client Lua does not support generators or yield. Keep state in ordinary functions and continue from lifecycle updates or timer callbacks.
lua_unsupportedNode: Client Lua cannot compile {{arg0}} syntax. Use ordinary functions and data operations, or import a native Lua module for Lua-specific code.
lua_unsupportedSyntax: Client Lua does not support async scheduling, generators, dynamic import or bigint. Use lifecycle hooks and regular numbers.
lua_truthiness: In Lua, 0 and empty strings are truthy. Compare explicitly, e.g. count !== 0 or name !== ''; use Boolean(value) for JavaScript conversion.
lua_nil: Lua nil removes table fields. In arrays it can create holes that affect length and iteration.

lua_unsupportedMember: Lua does not support standard library member {{arg0}}. Use a member from the Lua support list or a native API under lua.
lua_builtinMethodValue: Call Lua standard library methods directly on their object. For callbacks, use a function such as value => Math.abs(value).
lua_packageUnavailable: {{arg0}} cannot be used in Lua because it is implemented in JavaScript. Lua can import only this project's TS files, native modules with a matching .lua file, and genshin-ts/definitions/prefabs. Use lua.Enum for official enums.
lua_undefinedField: A field whose value is undefined does not exist in Lua (Object.keys will not see it either). If the field must always exist, give it an explicit value such as false or 0.
lua_arrayHole: Putting undefined in an array creates a hole in Lua, which breaks length and iteration. Keep array elements contiguous.
lua_deleteArray: Do not delete array elements. Use splice to remove elements and keep the array contiguous.
lua_bigint: Client Lua does not support bigint/BigInt. Use number and stay within the safe integer range.
lua_nativeTuple: When a native Lua function returns multiple values, type the return as LuaMultiReturn<[...]>. A plain tuple is treated as a single array, and destructuring will go wrong.
lua_nativeThis: Declare this: void on functions in native Lua objects; otherwise they compile to obj:fn(...) colon calls that pass one extra argument. If it really is a colon method, declare this: YourObjectType.
lua_modulo: Negative remainders differ from JS: -5 % 3 is -2 in JS but 1 in Lua. You can ignore this when neither side is negative; for the JS result, use lua.math.fmod(a, b). To hide this warning, set gsts/lua-modulo to 'off' in your ESLint config.
lua_enableSubscription: This subscribes in onEnable without keeping the cancel function, so every enable adds another listener and the callback runs repeatedly. Subscribe at the callback root instead (paused on disable, resumed on enable), or keep the cancel function and call it in onDisable.
